highlights: Anthropic explains how layered memory and offline "dreaming" help agents learn from past sessions; Mistral Studio adds managed agents, workflows and a Mistral MCP server.
Cloudflare open-sources an MIT-licensed security-audit skill, and Foundry Local now runs Qwen3.8-27B on GPUs with 24 GB of VRAM as a GitHub Copilot backend.

items.title: Anthropic explains agent memory and "dreaming"
items.summary: Anthropic describes dreaming, an offline pass where an agent reflects on its logs to fix mistakes and produce new notes and representations; the experiments ran on Claude Managed Agents. In one test, Claude's score rose from 54% to 61% as its wiki grew when it used both search and the wiki, versus 53% with search alone, while saving about 20,000 tokens per question. Developers building long-running agents get a concrete pattern for structuring and periodically consolidating memory.

evidence.quote: The same idea can help agents organize their memory by reflecting on logs to fix mistakes or produce new notes and representations. This process is often called dreaming (Figure 1).
We ran the CL-Bench 1.0 task using Claude Managed Agents .
When it used both search and the wiki, Claude’s aggregate score rose from 54% to 61% as that wiki grew, compared with 53% when it had access to the search tool alone.
Using search and the wiki also saved about 20,000 tokens per question.

items.title: Mistral Studio adds managed agents, workflows and an MCP server
items.summary: Mistral updated Studio with managed agents, workflows and enterprise context, and both models and platform can be deployed in your own cloud, VPC or on-premises. The new Mistral MCP server lets developers build with Mistral Vibe or their existing coding agent, test locally and deploy with one command, while OpenTelemetry traces show model calls, tool use and approvals. Enterprise teams that need self-hosted agents get runtime, deployment and debugging tooling around the models.

evidence.quote: New features like managed agents, workflows, and enterprise context streamline business processes, enabling faster development and deployment of AI solutions.
Deploy both the models and the platform in your own cloud, VPC or on-premises environment.
Through the new Mistral MCP server, developers can build with Mistral Vibe or the coding agent they already use, test locally and deploy to their Studio environment with one command.
OpenTelemetry traces show each step of a run, including model calls, tool use and approvals

items.title: Cloudflare open-sources a multi-phase security-audit agent skill
items.summary: Cloudflare released security-audit, an MIT-licensed skill that turns a coding agent into a multi-phase security auditor. Its core rule is that the agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it, and results are written to findings.json and validated against a schema; it needs a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents. Teams already using coding agents can install it to get independently verified, machine-readable audit findings.

evidence.quote: Adversarial validation. The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.
Structured output -- write confirmed , needs_validation , and rejected records to findings.json and validate them against report-schema.json .
A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents
License MIT -- see LICENSE .

items.title: Foundry Local runs Qwen3.8-27B locally for agentic coding
items.summary: Foundry Local can now run Qwen3.8-27B locally and connect it to GitHub Copilot: with 4-bit quantization the model is about 18 GB and fits consumer GPUs with 24 GB of VRAM at up to 64K tokens of context, or up to 262K tokens with 32 GB or more. It uses DFlash2 speculative decoding and requires Foundry Local CLI 0.13.0 or later. Developers with an NVIDIA GPU who want code to stay on their machine can try it today.

evidence.quote: Run Qwen3.8-27B locally, connect it to GitHub Copilot, and get a responsive coding experience with predictable inference costs, greater privacy, and the freedom to keep working offline.
With 4-bit quantization, the model size is reduced to approximately 18 GB, making it runnable on consumer GPUs with 24 GB of VRAM, supporting context windows of up to 64K tokens.
GPUs with 32 GB or more of VRAM can support longer context windows of up to the model’s maximum supported length of 262K tokens.
It leverages DFlash2 speculative decoding
This experience requires Foundry Local CLI 0.13.0 or later
Have an NVIDIA GPU with at least 24 GB of VRAM?

items.title: Nace AI opens the Drex family of decision models
items.summary: Drex is a family of four open decision models at 8B (DLM), 9B (v1.5), 35B with 3B active (v2.0) and 27B (Max) that take a state plus options and return a probability distribution over the options without autoregressive decoding. The paper reports that Max answers a typical request in 183 ms and trails Claude Opus 5.5 by 1.6 points on Decision Bench v4. For classification, judgment and scoring over fixed options, it avoids long chain-of-thought and output parsing.

evidence.quote: Max answers a typical request in 183 ms, against about 2.0 s for GPT-6 Sol and 3.5 s for Claude Opus 5.5, and its outputs are stable under option reordering . All four models are open source
On Decision Bench v4, it is statistically tied with d3-turbo and GPT-6 Sol and trails Claude Opus 5.5 by 1.6 points

items.title: Linum releases a 2B text-to-image model trained for about $21K
items.summary: Linum AI released P-JiT 21K, a 2B-parameter research checkpoint trained on 660M samples for about $21K of compute, under apache-2.0. Rendered-text images were filtered out on purpose, so it cannot write text or generate posters, and Linum calls it an experimental artifact rather than a production model. It is a useful reference point for anyone studying efficient image-model training.

evidence.quote: P-JiT 21K is a 2B-parameter model trained on 660M samples for about $21K of compute, as a stepping stone towards our next video model.
Research checkpoint: this is an experimental research artifact, not a production model.
This model cannot write text or generate posters.
License: apache-2.0

items.title: SLA builds spatial alignment into VLA continual pre-training
items.summary: SLA starts from a pretrained pi05 policy and jointly optimizes action prediction with alignment between intermediate visual embeddings and representations from a frozen 3D perception model. All auxiliary components are used only during training, so pretrained VLA weights can be reused and the inference architecture is unchanged. Robotics teams can adopt the training recipe without changing deployment.

evidence.quote: All auxiliary components are used only during training, allowing direct reuse of pretrained VLA weights and preserving the original inference architecture .

items.title: VFlash decodes whole visual plans in one forward pass
items.summary: Instead of generating boxes and trajectories one coordinate token at a time, VFlash uses a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass and directly accepts structurally valid predictions. Preliminary measurements show approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting, and a world action model conditioned on VFlash plans reaches 70.2% average success on MolmoSpaces versus 62.6% for the baseline. Systems that use VLMs for spatial planning in robotics or driving can cut decoding latency this way.

items.title: Harness-S trains agents by rescuing failures with sibling harnesses
items.summary: Harness-S evolves a pool of sibling harnesses that repair different failures, and only when all attempts under the base harness fail does the policy roll out again under selected siblings, with those trajectories replacing the failed group for reinforcement learning. Across AppWorld, SWE-Gym and DBBench, the trained policy substantially outperforms policy-only training when returned to the original base harness. Agent RL teams can fold harness improvements into the model itself.

evidence.quote: Across AppWorld, SWE-Gym, and DBBench, the trained policy substantially outperforms policy-only training when returned to the original base harness.

items.title: BestRand makes benchmark compression stable and cheap
items.summary: The paper shows that estimating full-benchmark scores from random subsets usually gives small errors but has a long tail of large ones, and proposes BestRand to cut that tail. Across 70+ text, multimodal and agent benchmarks, it reduces high-error risk by 50.2% and estimation error by 16.4% on average while requiring only 51.3% of the construction cost of competing methods. Teams on a tight eval budget can use it to pick small subsets instead of running full benchmarks.

evidence.quote: Across 70+ benchmarks, BestRand reduces high-error risk by 50.2% and estimation error by 16.4%, while requiring only 51.3% of the construction cost of competing methods.

items.title: Claude Code v2.1.319 runs MCP tasks in the background
items.summary: When an MCP server runs a tool call as a task, Claude Code now moves it to the background right away and tells Claude the result when it finishes, and a new permissions.denyInsteadOfPrompting setting denies tool calls that would wait on a permission prompt so the turn continues. Auto mode also changed with telemetry or feature flags off: calls the server can't check are asked about or denied, with no fallback to the built-in classifier. Teams running Claude Code behind gateways or unattended should review these behavior changes before upgrading.

items.title: llama.cpp merges Kimi-K3.1-Pro text model support
items.summary: llama.cpp merged PR #31779, adding text support for Kimi-K3.1-Pro; K3.1 reuses most of K3 but replaces the full-attention MLA layers with DSA. The vision tower and mm_projector are skipped for now, so it is text only. Users with enough hardware can now run the model locally with llama.cpp.

evidence.quote: K3.1 reuses most of K3, but replaces the full-attention MLA layers with DSA.
the vision tower and mm_projector are skipped: text only for now

items.title: Apple speeds up RAG retrieval with small learned networks
items.summary: In an ICML 2026 paper, Apple researchers train small neural networks once, offline, for a fixed database of keys so queries are routed toward their best match faster: SupportNet handles cluster routing, and KeyNet can act as a query rewriter in front of a standard IVF index. Reaching 99% recall takes up to ~8× less time with the largest KeyNet model (0.23 ms vs 1.8 ms). RAG and recommendation systems with a fairly stable key set can trade offline training for lower query latency.

evidence.quote: In Amortizing Maximum Inner Product Search with Learned Support Functions , a paper presented at ICML 2026, researchers from Apple train small neural networks (NNs) — once, offline, for a fixed database of keys — that learn how to route queries toward their best match faster.
The SupportNet neural network architecture can learn the support function directly
KeyNet works naturally as a “query rewriter” in front of a standard approximate search index
reaching 99% recall takes up to ~8× less time with the largest model (0.23 ms vs 1.8 ms for the raw query)
With KeyNet, we can also keep the IVF system as is and just feed it a modified version of the query.

items.title: Anthropic studies how scientists use Claude
items.summary: Analyzing 207,000 research sessions, Anthropic finds scientists primarily use Claude to analyze data and to write, and computer science accounts for 32.7% of Claude Code sessions.

evidence.quote: Scientists primarily use Claude to analyze data and to write.
Despite making up only 4.3% of the world’s researchers, computer science alone accounts for 32.7% of Claude Code sessions.

items.title: OpenAI introduces the BioBasicsBench wet-lab benchmark
items.summary: OpenAI's BioBasicsBench is a 100-task benchmark measuring how well AI agents interpret raw experimental data and handle everyday wet-lab science.

items.title: WeLM-Image unifies image generation for single-GPU deployment
items.summary: WeLM-Image combines multimodal understanding with text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing and multi-reference synthesis, with 31.7B stored parameters and approximately 5.4B generation parameters activated per target latent token.

items.title: Meta adds spaces to the Muse app
items.summary: Meta's new spaces let Muse users describe an idea and have Muse build a custom experience they can keep adjusting as they use it.
